outcome: No mathematical progress on Norton's Generalized Moonshine Conjecture was found in the window 26 January 2024 to present; the conjecture's status is unchanged from before the frozen revision.

disputes.summary: Sources disagree on whether Scott Carnahan's 'Generalized Moonshine I-IV' series (2008-2012) plus Carnahan-Miyamoto's non-Fricke work (2016) constitute a full resolution of Norton's Generalized Moonshine Conjecture, or only a resolution of the hardest remaining cases (Fricke and non-Fricke elements) leaving other aspects unconfirmed by experts. The Encyclopedia of Mathematics (last substantively updated ~2023) states flatly that 'only special cases of these generalized moonshine conjectures have been proven,' citing Dong-Li-Mason (cyclic case) and Höhn (2A involution case) as examples, and does not describe Carnahan's work as a complete resolution. Other secondary sources (Wikipedia's Monstrous moonshine article, various summaries) describe Carnahan's Fricke-element result as 'resolving' or 'establishing the remaining open claims in' the conjecture. This dispute entirely predates the 26 January 2024 window and does not change the analysis here, since no source dates any resolution (partial or complete) to within the window regardless of which reading is correct.

summary: I searched extensively for any post-26-January-2024 developments on Norton's Generalized Moonshine Conjecture and found none. The mathematical literature on generalized moonshine itself is essentially quiet in this window. The one arXiv result with a 2606.xxxx identifier that surfaced in search ('Moonshine: An Autonomous Mathematical Research Agent Centered on Conjecture Generation,' arXiv:2606.10806) is a false lead: I opened it directly and confirmed it is an unrelated AI-agent paper that happens to be named 'Moonshine' and works on a self-invented 'Neural Jacobian Conjecture' about neural network injectivity — it has no connection to the monster group or generalized moonshine in the group-theoretic/VOA sense, and I am discarding it from consideration. The one arguably relevant 2024-2026 item involving AI is a GitHub issue (google-deepmind/formal-conjectures#2149, opened 2026-02-03) in which an AI agent (attributed to a human account 'franzhusch,' with the issue footer stating 'This issue was generated by an AI agent and reviewed by me') logged Norton's Generalized Moonshine as a candidate for future Lean formalization, rating it '5/5' difficulty and noting prerequisite infrastructure (Monster group, graded VOA representations, modular form theory) that does not yet exist in Mathlib. This produced no mathematics whatsoever — no proof, no formalization, no conjecture, not even a partial Lean statement — only a scoping/cataloguing note, so it does not constitute an 'event' under this schema and I have left `event` null and `ai_role` as `none` (the agent did not produce any part of a mathematical result). The Duncan-Harvey-Rayhaun paper on 'Two New Avatars of Moonshine for the Thompson Group' (arXiv:2202.08277, last revised May 2025) is about Thompson moonshine, a related but distinct moonshine phenomenon for the Thompson sporadic group, not Norton's Generalized Moonshine Conjecture for the Monster stated in this bullet, so under the scope rule (§3.1) it is a related problem, not a case of this one, and does not count. The triage record's assessment is correct: the substantive resolution work (Carnahan's Generalized Moonshine I-IV, 2008-2012, and Carnahan-Miyamoto 2016 on non-Fricke elements) all predates the frozen revision by 8-16 years, so even setting aside the dispute over whether that work fully resolves the conjecture, there is no post-window event to date and the correct status is `open` (not `open_stale`, since I could not confirm from primary/expert sources that a full resolution — as opposed to resolution of the hardest special cases — occurred at all, even before 2024). I checked the problem's Wikipedia article family (Monstrous moonshine), the Encyclopedia of Mathematics entry (updated as recently as 2023, still describing only special cases as proven), arXiv listings and topical searches for 2024-2026, and found nothing that changes what a careful person would write in this bullet.
competing_reading: If one takes the (contested) position that Carnahan's 2008-2016 work already fully resolved Norton's conjecture, then the correct status would be `open_stale` rather than `open`, since the resolution event predates the frozen revision. I did not adopt this reading because the Encyclopedia of Mathematics — a more authoritative, actively-maintained secondary source than the popular science and Wikipedia summaries — explicitly states only special cases are proven and does not describe Carnahan's results as a complete resolution. This is a genuine unresolved dispute in how the field is described, but it does not change the answer for this exercise since no source, on either reading, places a resolution event inside the 26 January 2024 - present window.
what_would_settle_it: An authoritative statement from an expert in vertex operator algebra / moonshine (e.g., a current survey, a statement from Carnahan himself, or an update to the Encyclopedia of Mathematics or Wikipedia's Monstrous moonshine article) clarifying whether the 2008-2016 Carnahan/Carnahan-Miyamoto series is considered by the community to fully resolve Norton's Generalized Moonshine Conjecture (which would make this open_stale) or leaves a residual open piece (which would keep it open, as recorded). Separately, any future arXiv preprint or announcement specifically addressing generalized moonshine (not Thompson, Mathieu, or umbral moonshine, which are distinct phenomena) would be the kind of event that could change this record.
